doc.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019

title: Western Kentucky University, Bowling Green gig and senior recital
summary: He chose Western Kentucky on Cannonball's advice, worked a five-night gig, studied counterpoint with Claude Rose, and learned to finish a job through his senior recital.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I wanted to not go to college and just play, but my parents really balked at that and so my dad insisted that I go to college. And so my grades went — I was working for some obscure college up in the mountains someplace, and I happened to choose Western Kentucky University. And Cannonball was going, “Man, when I was stationed at Ft. Knox I used to go there and take private composition lessons with Roy Harris. He was the head of the department there.” He said, “It’s a great school because” he said, “there’s very few music majors and you’ll be like getting private lessons with like three people in the class.” So I went there and I graduated. I went there four years. And I paid my own way through college because I was playing a gig five nights a week.
Was the music that you played on those gigs different than you played in Florida?
Of course. Man, you remember Ace Denning?

He would sing “Annie’s cousin Fanny” and those kind of tunes. I hated the gig but it was paying my way through school. But I was working five nights a week and carrying — I did four years, it would have took five years, and playing that gig too. But the music, I already knew most of that stuff man. Some of the teachers would come ask me stuff you know. And so the music study was easy except for I did learn an awful lot about counterpoint and stuff like that. And you know that drilling, every day, every day. There was one class you took for four years, three hours from nine to noon, with this wonderful teacher by the name of Claude Rose. He’s dead now. But it was four part contrapuntal harmonic technique. And so I got an awful lot out of that. And the discipline of — when I

say I can get a job finished you know what that’s from? Having to play a senior recital to graduate. So I spent that whole year, my whole senior year, practicing for that recital. I played a Bach French suite, six movements, I played a Hindemith sonata, and a Chopin ballad. And so I was practicing for the whole year and then playing that concert and getting through it successfully enabled me to get a job finished. So like when I came to New York doing stuff like writing those arrangements, I can get the job done.
